The '''Tahiti Ligue 1''' is the top division of the [[Fédération Tahitienne de Football]] in [[French Polynesia]]. The league is currently named '''Ligue 1 Vini''' for sponsorship reasons.

==Competition format==
The competition is divided into a regular season and play-offs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/national/tahiti/super-ligue-mana/2011-2012/championship-round/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160402065549/http://int.soccerway.com/national/tahiti/super-ligue-mana/2011-2012/championship-round/r16975/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 2, 2016 |title=Summary - Ligue 1 - Tahiti - Results, fixtures, tables and news - Soccerway |website=Uk.soccerway.com |date=2013-01-09 |access-date=2016-06-24}}</ref> The regular season is a league format. At the end of the regular season the top six teams&nbsp;– and in past seasons the winners of the [[Moorea]] island league&nbsp;– enter a play-off league to determine the overall champions and qualifiers for the [[OFC Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ftf.pf/?page_id%3D996%26pagename%3DClassements |title=FTF » Classements |access-date=March 2, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130918135540/http://www.ftf.pf/?page_id=996 |archive-date=September 18, 2013 }}</ref> Meanwhile, the lower teams enter a separate play-off league along with teams from [[Tahiti Ligue 2|Ligue 2]] to determine promotion and relegation for the following season.

The league has a point scoring system whereby teams are awarded 4 points for a win, 2 points for a draw and 1 point for a defeat. The only way a team cannot score a point is by failing to field a team. Although it is not unique, and is inspired from the [[French Football Federation|French]] ranking system for every division below the [[Championnat de France Amateur#Competition format|third tier]], as well as the women's league (all before 2016), it has received publicity when the [[Tahiti national football team]] qualified for the [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup|Confederations Cup]]. According to an interview with Charles Ariitoma, the President of the [[Fédération Tahitienne de Football|FTF]], this was introduced because "we don't want anyone to be sad".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/blogs/early-doors/tahitian-league-offers-one-point-loss-nobody-sad-130923208.html |title=Tahitian League gives one point for a loss 'so nobody's sad' &#124; Early Doors - Yahoo Sport |website=Uk.eurosport.yahoo.com |date=2013-10-13 |access-date=2016-06-24 |archive-date=2015-02-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150207003603/https://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/blogs/early-doors/tahitian-league-offers-one-point-loss-nobody-sad-130923208.html |url-status=live }}</ref>
